candidates.application: one vsetvl-driven strip loop per row pass; the tail is a smaller vl

candidates.title: Box sums by sliding adds
candidates.application: horizontal 5-sums of pixels and squares from five shifted loads (or slides), vertical sums from five row buffers kept in a ring; never recompute 25 products per pixel
candidates.expected_gain: each box sum is 4 adds per direction instead of 25 multiply-accumulates

candidates.title: x_by_x lookup by an indexed load or an in-register gather
candidates.application: z is at most 255: vluxei8 from dav1d_sgr_x_by_x, or keep the 256-byte table in an LMUL-4 register group at VLEN 512 and use vrgather.vv with the 8-bit z as index
candidates.expected_gain: replaces scalar table loads; in-register gather avoids memory latency
preconditions: indices clamped to 0..255 before the lookup

candidates.title: p*s with the C's 32-bit wrap
candidates.application: z = (p*s + (1<<19)) >> 20 must wrap at 32 bits: use e32 vmul (modular) and a logical vsrl, never a widening multiply
candidates.expected_gain: correctness: 25*sumsq up to 1.6e6 makes p*s exceed 2^32 for the legal s range

candidates.application: pixels widen u8 -> u16 -> u32 once per tap and stay in widened registers across the box-sum, weight and finish stages instead of re-widening
run the per-row passes at the largest LMUL the register budget allows (box rows and finish rows are independent across x)
preconditions: group bases stay aligned; widening source EMUL matches how data was written
